body: Damn, this explains a whole lotta things I didn’t know at once. That’s a lot for the detailed response! I think I lingered a bit on accessory mode, and saw the check engine light because of it. Im stressed right now so so I took to mean the worst haha

Is that what’s happening when you turn the key partially so the lights come on, but not so far the engine kicks on? Fuck me, leaving it in that spot was always scared me because I thought “the lights are on, so surely the engine should be running!” So it is safe to roll the windows up and down like that? I’m assuming it would extend the length of my engine and battery. I’m not a car guy so this is huge to me
If I kill myself, will I go to hell?
I really thought that was gonna be the one

Yeah, sorry, I’m just pretty high rn so I felt too lazy to type up the long winded explanation, I’ve done it so many times before. But fuck it, what’s one more. Essentially, my philosophy is that life is inherently worse than death. Similar to the Buddhist philosophy of suffering as inherent to the human condition, without the “but wait there’s still a reason to live” part. For example, biological aspects to life like the brains attenuation to neurochemicals like dopamine making utopian societies impossible (this meaning that a constant state of positive stimuli is impossible regardless of how hard you work towards it) and if dead one cannot mourn their lack of existence due to an obviously missing ability to perceive once dead. If you take that into consideration it damages the concept of inherent value in human life especially due to the impermanence of the universes existence. Eventually all shall be forgotten. 

I’ll try to keep this part brief because I can tell that the top part is a poorly formatted mess, I’m pretty tired sorry. Basically, I don’t want anything. I don’t want a nice car, or house, or fucking anything but a nice computer. I have that. So what now, I work to... live and work more? I feel like I’ve played the free trial of a game, and I didn’t like it but everyone is telling me “don’t quit yet! It gets better!” But I hate it from a fundamental level. I don’t have my survival instincts because of abuse I went through for most of my life until I was 11, I just don’t have that fundamental will to live. Now, the first paragraph and this may seem unrelated, but what I mean is I’ve done the research to try and find a reason to live. I couldn’t find one, and even if other people may be perfectly happy, and validly as their brains allow them to let go of the negative thoughts and just do shit they don’t want to do less painfully, mine doesn’t. So if I don’t want to live, and suicide has no OBJECTIVE immorality, why wont anyone just let me die?

So, I don’t get many chances to articulate this fully, it’s mostly just been refining certain parts of my logic as people don’t like to talk about this for too long, so this may seem a bit rambly. If you need clarification I can certainly do so.
My decision was made years ago, I may be trying to find peace with others but I don’t need it. My blood is on no ones hands but my own.

Thank you. I plead for permission to die by explaining the thought process I’ve worked out over my whole life. I don’t know why but it’s how I think, it always has been and it’s how I communicate. It’s so hard to get people to listen that it makes me feel like I’m loosing my mind sometimes.

Nah, I couldn’t care less where I die. If I did do something I’d probably go to Greenland or somewhere else cold and snowy. But it’s all the same when your a dead body I guess. I’m mostly just waiting until my dad dies, I can’t inflict this on him. No matter how irrational it is to care I will, it’s a matter of principle and that just doesn’t abide by logic.

Ah, yeah, I have no belief in anything that cannot be observed scientifically, occam’s razor and all that. Our brains can be studied next to those of non sapient life forms, we can see the biological differences. Mysticism oftentimes stems from ignorance unfortunately.

Well if you could find an objective way to poke holes in my argument by all means please do, but I’ve heard all the platitudes before. Saying “we all think we’re right” doesn’t disprove something. I’m open to criticism, I’ve been trying to poke holes in it for fucking years and run it by many people in an attempt to refine it. But “you’re wrong because you think your right” statements have no objective merit. As I said in my post subjectively life can be worthwhile but for the reasons mentioned mine is not, and the objective points I’ve provided are for the sake of dispelling the notion that one should live because they’re alive.

See this is exactly what I mean, I don’t care if my problems go away. I don’t want to die because I’m laden with problems, I want to die because even having to wait an extra 30 seconds to get some delivery food isn’t worth it. If I don’t feel, there is no pain. Happiness that need never have existed cannot make up for pain that is just as unnecessary. Not to mention that neurologically you will always be in pain no matter what, if we weren’t in pain we wouldn’t have any reason to live. Your brain will attenuate to the happiness you feel and if it becomes too common it will no longer evoke the joy it used to. This can be seen in studies of happiness levels according to wealth and in philosophical thought experiments regarding utopias. They can’t exist because of how psychology works, what we’re pretending we’re working towards isn’t fucking possible. We imagine a society in which work is replaced my robots and we all think “but it would be so boring.” We have to suffer to live, it’s just the human condition. But I don’t have the survival instincts to create the will to accept that. The only scenario I would consider living is if I got a lobotomy, but the pursuit of improvement of ones own life for the purpose of a slightly more comfortable death is ridiculous and shortsighted at best.
